::: {#def-vector-derivative}
#### Vector derivative (gradient)
If $f(\vcoef)$ is a scalar-valued function of a $p \times 1$ vector $\vcoef$,
such as $f(\vcoef) = \dprod{\vx}{\vcoef}$,
then its **vector derivative** is the column vector of its
partial derivatives (@def-partial-derivative):

$$
\deriv{ \vcoef} f(\vcoef) =
\sbmat{
\deriv{\coef{1}}f(\vcoef) \\
\deriv{\coef{2}}f(\vcoef) \\
\vdots \\
\deriv{\coef{p}}f(\vcoef)
}
$$

The vector derivative is also called the **gradient** of $f$ with respect to $\vcoef$,
written $\nabla_{\vcoef} f(\vcoef)$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-vector-derivative}
#### A vector derivative

Let $\vcoef = \tp{(\coef{1}, \coef{2})}$ and $f(\vcoef) = 3 \coef{1} + 5 \coef{2}^2$. Then

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef} f(\vcoef)}_{2 \times 1}
= \sbmat{
\deriv{\coef{1}} (3 \coef{1} + 5 \coef{2}^2) \\
\deriv{\coef{2}} (3 \coef{1} + 5 \coef{2}^2)
}
= \sbmat{ 3 \\ 10 \coef{2} },
$$

and at $\vcoef = \tp{(1, 2)}$ the vector derivative is $\tp{(3, 20)}$.

:::
